title.en: BB06.4 Introduction to body defence mechanisms
title.zhHant: BB06.4 身體防禦機制簡介

items.stem: The main purpose of vaccination is to

options.text: kill all bacteria in the body immediately.
replace white blood cells with antibiotics.
create immune memory so the body can respond quickly if the same pathogen invades later.
increase blood glucose so white blood cells work faster.

items.hint: Review 6.4 Introduction to body defence mechanisms.

items.stem: After a vaccine is given, white blood cells

options.text: recognise the vaccine material and produce antibodies.
store fat as adipose tissue.
produce insulin.
deposit cholesterol in arteries.

items.hint: Review 6.4 Introduction to body defence mechanisms.

options.text: digest starch in the gut.
remember the pathogen so a later infection can be fought more quickly.
transmit the pathogen to other people.
cause type 1 diabetes.

items.hint: Review 6.4 Introduction to body defence mechanisms.

items.stem: A COVID-19 vaccine introduces a viral protein into the body. Which sequence is correct?

options.text: memory cells form → antibodies produced → vaccine given
pathogen kills all white blood cells → vaccine given → memory cells form
antibodies are taken as tablets → memory cells form in the gut
vaccine given → immune system produces antibodies → memory cells form

items.hint: Review 6.4 Introduction to body defence mechanisms.

items.stem: After vaccination, if the person is later infected by the same pathogen,

options.text: no antibodies can be produced.
a large amount of antibodies can be produced quickly, helping to kill the pathogens.
the person must develop cancer.
insulin sensitivity is reduced.

items.hint: Review 6.4 Introduction to body defence mechanisms.

items.stem: Which of the following are used to prevent infectious disease by preparing the immune system in advance?

options.text: (1) and (2) only
(1) and (3) only
(2) and (3) only

items.hint: Review 6.4 Introduction to body defence mechanisms.
items: eating less lipid to prevent atherosclerosis

items.stem: Which of the following statements about vaccines is incorrect?

options.text: Vaccines must contain live pathogens that cause a full disease in every person.
A vaccine may contain fragments or a dead pathogen.
Immune memory allows a faster response when the corresponding pathogen invades.
White blood cells are involved in recognising the vaccine material.

items.hint: Review 6.4 Introduction to body defence mechanisms.

items.stem: Person X received a vaccine. Person Y has never been vaccinated or infected. Both are then exposed to the same virus. Which prediction is most reasonable?

options.text: Only Y can produce antibodies.
X and Y produce the same amount of antibodies at the same speed.
X is more likely to produce a large amount of antibodies quickly because of memory cells.
Vaccination makes X unable to produce antibodies.

items.hint: Review 6.4 Introduction to body defence mechanisms.

items.stem: HPV vaccination reduces the risk of cervical cancer. This example shows that

options.text: cervical cancer is spread by mosquito bites.
preventing an infectious virus can lower the risk of a non-infectious disease (cancer).
all non-infectious diseases can be prevented by vaccines.
cancer is caused by lack of insulin.
